headline: XPENG'S ROBOT
STARTS **JAN 2027**
cover.hook_pick_reason: No reader-impact hook: the only price signal is Gu's expectation that Iron will cost about as much as an Xpeng car (119,800 yuan, about $18,000, to 309,800 yuan); no fixed price, buyer segment or home availability is announced, and household chores are one executive's estimate, so that label would overpromise. The headline is the best-supported fact: Xpeng says production of Iron starts in January 2027, which slides 1 to 3 back directly and which says production starts, not that volume is built. The 2.5-minute option is a design capacity, not an output rate, and needs a qualifier the cover cannot carry; 'tens of thousands' is a sales aim; the chores option is one executive's estimate.

slides.title: A car maker goes humanoid
body: Xpeng, a Chinese EV maker, says it will start mass-producing its Iron humanoid robot in **January 2027**. It will train the robot as a store assistant first.

slides.title: Chores in one or two years
body: Co-president Brian Gu told CNBC the robot could be doing household chores in **"one or two years."** He expects a car-like price: Xpeng cars cost 119,800 yuan (about $18,000) to 309,800 yuan. No fixed price is announced.

slides.title: Built on Xpeng's car tech
body: Iron has **76 degrees of freedom** and more than 1,500 touch sensors. It runs on three of Xpeng's own Turing AI chips, the same family it puts in its cars.

slides.title: One robot every 2.5 minutes
body: Xpeng's new production line is **designed to** finish one robot every 2.5 minutes at full speed. That is a design target, not a reported output.

slides.title: Tens of thousands in 2027
body: Gu told Bloomberg TV Xpeng **aims to sell** "tens of thousands" of Iron robots in 2027, with public sales from the second quarter. Its robotics unit raised more than **$900M** in August.

slides.title: China's humanoid year
body: Morgan Stanley expects China to ship **50,000 humanoids** this year, across all makers, not just Xpeng. The Next Web gives no background on that estimate.

facts.text: Chinese EV maker Xpeng will start mass-producing its Iron humanoid robot in January 2027 and train it as a store assistant first.
Co-president Brian Gu told CNBC it could be doing household chores in "one or two years."
The robot has 76 degrees of freedom and more than 1,500 touch sensors.
It runs on three of Xpeng's own Turing AI chips, the same family it puts in its cars.
Xpeng's new production line is designed to finish one every 2.5 minutes at full speed.
Xpeng aims to sell "tens of thousands" of Iron robots in 2027, with public sales from the second quarter, Gu told Bloomberg TV.
Xpeng's robotics unit raised more than $900M in August ahead of the production run.
Morgan Stanley expects China to ship 50,000 humanoids this year.
Gu expects Iron to cost about as much as one of Xpeng's cars, which sell for 119,800 yuan (about $18,000) to 309,800 yuan.

sources.title: Xpeng says its Iron humanoid could be doing chores in one or two years

caption:
Xpeng, the Chinese EV maker, says it will start mass-producing its Iron humanoid robot in January 2027.

The Next Web relays interviews with co-president Brian Gu on CNBC and Bloomberg TV. These are company statements and goals, not results. Gu expects a car-like price, but no fixed price is announced.

→ Production starts January 2027, with the robot trained as a store assistant first
→ Gu expects a price near an Xpeng car (119,800 yuan, about $18,000, to 309,800 yuan), not yet fixed
→ Xpeng aims to sell "tens of thousands" in 2027, with public sales from Q2
